⚽ Football Scouting Dashboard – Young Strikers

A medium-sized club with a limited budget wants a young, talented and affordable player. This dashboard presents the notebook analysis and lets you test it yourself.

17,954players in the dataset (51 columns, 0 duplicate rows)
1.42%missing market value (255 players)
1,069players aged 23 or younger with potential 80+
13strikers passing all filters

Data quality: what is missing?

Only a few columns have gaps. Market value and wage matter most, because the cost estimate needs both.

Missing market values by age group

Gaps are small in every group. Among young high-potential players only 4 are missing (0.37%), and their average potential (82.75) is almost identical to the rest (82.78).

Data quality decisions

  • All players stay in the original dataset.
  • Missing values are excluded only from analyses that need them.
  • Missing market values are never replaced with zero, which would make players look free.
  • Players missing value or wage are left out of the financial analysis, since their cost cannot be calculated reliably. They can still be scouted.

Market value segments: all players vs. young players (23 and under)

Segments: low up to €3M, medium €3–10M, high above €10M. Young players are 6,745 of the 17,699 players with a value.

Higher value means higher ratings, which is expected because value is largely driven by rating and potential. The low-value pool is big (5,998) but its average rating is only 60.6, so the club needs extra filters on potential, current ability and wage instead of buying by price alone.

Limitations

  • FIFA video game data, not verified real-world scouting data.
  • Market values and wages are game estimates, not actual fees or salaries.
  • Scouting weights are assumptions for a counter-attacking style and were not validated on real matches.
  • Injuries, contracts, availability and match statistics are not included.

Why these filters?

The thresholds are illustrative business assumptions for a hypothetical medium-sized club, not verified club requirements. Changing them would change the shortlist.

FilterWhy it was chosenPlayers left
Age ≤ 23Young players have room to grow and can gain resale value.–
Potential ≥ 80Keeps only players projected to become strong, which is the goal of a future-focused signing.1,065
Market value ≤ €3MAssumed affordability limit for a limited budget. Players at exactly €3M count as low value.442
Weekly wage ≤ €10KCaps salary commitment (about €520K a year). D. Oberlin sits exactly on this limit.395
Overall ≥ 68Ensures the player can contribute now. This is the strictest filter and removes 286 players.109
Position includes STAssumed club need: a striker for a counter-attacking style.13

Counts start from young players with potential 80+ who have both value and wage data (1,065 of 1,069).

Tune the model

Change the weights to match the playing style (counter-attack) and the cost cap. Scores and ranking update instantly.

Weights are normalized to 100%. Cost = market value + weekly wage × 52 × 3 (an estimate, not a real transfer fee).

Score vs. cost

A good player sits high and to the left. Green players form the efficiency frontier among the players within your budget: none of them is beaten by another eligible striker with a higher score at a lower cost. Circle size = potential. Faded players are over budget (dashed line = cap). Hover or tap a player for details.

Striker ranking

"Efficient" = efficiency frontier among players within the current budget.
